THE ONE OPERATOR STEP: run `cc-permission-audit --prune` on the box. BARE - do NOT name a path and do NOT set CONFIRM=1. Naming a settings.json path IS the rewrite authorization (tests/cc-permission-dropped.bats "a DISCOVERED settings.json is reported but never rewritten without being named"); bare it reports across every ~/.claude*/ store and can mutate nothing. The drop list is report-only by design regardless: an auto-dropped rule is restored on leaving auto mode, so it is dead WEIGHT, not a dead ENTRY. Read the output in this order: (1) the classifyAllShell banner FIRST - if autoMode.classifyAllShell is true in ANY store, EVERY Bash allow rule is inert in auto mode and the per-entry count is moot, not merely longer (permission-matcher-truth-2026-08-20.md F10); (2) the "N of 339 ... DROPPED before matching in auto mode" line - that N is the item's answer; (3) the redundancy count, the only axis --prune ever removes. Remedy for anything listed is to NARROW (Bash(npm run test:*) survives; Bash(npm run:*) does not), never to delete.

CHANNEL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED on this branch (d5f2d0b5) - read this before trusting any past `cc-bus fold --refs` all-clear. The shipped default ref glob was `refs/remotes/*`, which git for-each-ref matches with wildmatch under WM_PATHNAME where a single `*` does not cross a `/`. Every remote-tracking ref is at least refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>, and a cloud worker's is deeper (refs/remotes/origin/claude/fire-...), so the default matched ZERO refs - measured 0 vs 307 on this clone. `fold --refs` is the ONLY documented path by which the box reads an off-box worker's records, so cloud->local read has been a SILENT NO-OP on the default: it printed nothing and exited 0, which reads as "no records" rather than as "did not look". Fixed to `refs/remotes/**`; reproduced end-to-end from a checkout at origin/main both ways.

Why the suite never caught it: both existing --refs tests pin CC_BUS_REF_GLOB=refs/heads/* - one segment deep, so they match under the broken pattern too and the bug is unreachable from them. Added a test that pins NO glob and asserts the shipped default against a real remote-tracking ref with a slashed branch name; it fails on `*` at the payload assertion and passes on `**`. Same class the cc-bus header already warns about for CC_BUS_ACTOR - every check pinning the variable it should have been testing. tests/cc-bus.bats 37/37, cc-bus --selftest 22/22.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DRAIN BRIDGE, not fixed here and worth a decision: cmd_drain takes only --apply and --to - it rejects --refs and has no way to set BUS_FOLD_REFS, so `drain --apply` reads the WORKTREE only. Even with this glob fix, an off-box record still cannot reach the local stores until its branch is merged. So the two halves of the documented flow disagree: `fold --refs` can read across refs, `drain` cannot. Until that is closed, merging the worker branch is a prerequisite for drain, not an optimization.
